summary.business_type: YMYL content publisher + freemium SaaS tool (Canadian-immigration eligibility calculators/quiz for Brazilians; monetized via a R$19.90 one-time AI-generated report and a R$29.90/mo subscription)
top_findings: The blog's backend API is broken in production right now: /api/blog returns [] and /api/blog/{slug} returns 404, so every one of the 90 blog URLs (30% of the site) shows a full 'Erro ao carregar artigo' error page to real visitors and to any JS-rendering crawler, even though the raw server-rendered HTML (what most SEO tools check) still looks fine.

The entire site runs on a soft-404 architecture: any nonexistent URL, plus four real sitemapped pages (/faq, /templates, /comparador, /prontidao), return HTTP 200 with the homepage's exact title/description/canonical/JSON-LD in raw HTML, only correcting client-side after full JS hydration.

Critical E-E-A-T/trust gaps for a YMYL, money-collecting site: no About page anywhere, no named authors (Article schema uses a bare Organization), no Organization schema at all, and the 'we are not a licensed RCIC/immigration consultant' disclaimer is buried in Terms of Service and a collapsed FAQ answer instead of being shown on /precos at the point of payment.

A live factual contradiction: /programas/pnp_ontario still states the Ontario PNP is 'Status: Ativo' with open streams, while /pnp/ontario and a blog post correctly report OINP was revoked 30 May 2026 (confirmed against external sources) — a user could land on either page and get the opposite answer.

100% of blog posts (90/90) ship with an empty meta description / og:description / twitter:description, and the sitemap's lastmod is fabricated (stamped 'today') on 204 of 294 URLs (69%), both of which are pure execution bugs, not design limitations.
quick_wins: Backfill meta description / og:description / twitter:description on all 90 blog posts (templated fix, one bug covers all 90 pages)
Add a visible, non-collapsed disclaimer on /precos and at checkout: 'Relatório gerado por IA; não somos consultores licenciados (RCIC/CICC)'
Fix the raw-HTML SSR metadata for /faq, /comparador, /prontidao, /templates so each serves its own title/description/canonical instead of the homepage's
Correct the 'Status: Ativo' factual error on /programas/pnp_ontario to reflect the actual May 2026 OINP revocation
Remove the duplicate /noc/72410 sitemap entry and stop stamping lastmod with today's date on every non-blog URL
Add X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN (or CSP frame-ancestors) — trivial, closes a clickjacking gap on a payment-taking site
Add Service/Offer JSON-LD to /precos and WebApplication/Offer schema to /calculadora-crs — currently zero structured data on the two highest-commercial-value pages on the site

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: HTTPS everywhere with HSTS (preload + includeSubDomains), correct www→apex 301, X-Content-Type-Options, Permissions-Policy, and strict-origin-when-cross-origin referrer policy
robots.txt is well-formed, correctly disallows private/app routes, and declares the sitemap
The large majority of templates (blog, NOC, programas, PNP, custo-de-vida, tools) are genuinely server-rendered with unique per-route meta in raw HTML — this is not a thin SPA site
Mobile viewport meta and PWA manifest/apple-touch tags present and correct on every template sampled
ads.txt correctly implemented and consistent with the AdSense verification tag

findings.title: Any non-existent URL, plus /faq, /templates, /comparador, /prontidao, return HTTP 200 with the homepage's raw title/description/canonical/JSON-LD (soft-404)
findings.description: curl against a deliberately invented URL returns byte-identical HTML to the real homepage (same title, meta description, canonical, and WebSite/FAQPage/Offer/SoftwareApplication JSON-LD), with HTTP 200 and meta robots 'index, follow'. The same defect hits four real, sitemapped, unique pages — their genuine content only appears after full client-side JS hydration. Only after render does the app correct itself, and even then, stale homepage JSON-LD isn't cleared from the DOM.
findings.recommendation: Have the server return a real 404 (or 410) status for unknown routes before falling back to the SPA shell; add the four affected routes to whatever mechanism injects per-route SSR metadata; treat this as a regression test for all future routes.

findings.title: Plain HTTP (port 80) dead-ends on a bare 404 instead of redirecting to HTTPS
findings.description: Both http://immigracan.com.br/ and http://www.immigracan.com.br/ return a plain-text 404 with no redirect, unlike the working https://www→apex 301. This breaks old bookmarks, print/QR links, non-browser clients, and any http:// backlink.
findings.recommendation: Add/fix the HTTP-only nginx server block to 301-redirect to the HTTPS canonical, preserving path and query.

findings.title: 100% of blog posts (90/90) ship an empty meta description, og:description, and twitter:description
findings.description: Systematically confirmed across every blog URL in the sitemap. Every other template (homepage, tools, programas, PNP, custo-de-vida, NOC, imigrar-como) has a correctly populated description; this is isolated to the blog template, likely a null CMS field with no excerpt fallback.
findings.recommendation: Backfill descriptions for all 90 posts (auto-generate from first ~155 characters as a fallback), and fix the template so new posts don't ship empty.

findings.title: Blog og:image/twitter:image use root-relative URLs instead of absolute (inconsistent with homepage)
findings.description: Every sampled blog post uses a relative path like /blog/{slug}.png for og:image while the homepage correctly uses an absolute URL. Many WhatsApp/Telegram/Slack/email unfurlers won't resolve relative OG image URLs, breaking link-preview images on the platform this audience shares content through most.
findings.recommendation: Emit fully-qualified absolute URLs for og:image/twitter:image on every template.

findings.title: Overlapping /pnp/{province} and /programas/pnp_{code} URL structures compete for the same programs
findings.description: Both structures exist, both self-canonicalize, both target the same real-world program (e.g. Ontario) with different framing (news/status vs. requirements reference) but overlapping keyword space, splitting authority and confusing which is canonical.
findings.recommendation: Cross-link each pair explicitly, or consolidate into one canonical page per province with a dated status module.

findings.title: Sitemap lastmod is fabricated for 204 of 294 URLs (69%); blog lastmod is genuinely accurate
findings.description: Every non-blog URL — tools, programas, PNP, NOC (86 pages), custo-de-vida, the homepage itself — shows lastmod stamped to today's date regardless of real changes. The 90 blog posts, by contrast, show real differentiated dates matching their own Article JSON-LD dateModified exactly.
findings.recommendation: Only update lastmod when underlying content actually changes; Google may start ignoring lastmod sitewide (including the blog's currently-trustworthy values) if this persists.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options header
findings.description: The security header baseline is otherwise strong (HSTS, nosniff, Permissions-Policy), but there's no clickjacking protection and no CSP despite third-party scripts (GTM, AdSense, Fonts) and a payment/checkout flow.
findings.recommendation: Add X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN immediately (low effort); introduce CSP incrementally starting in Report-Only mode.

findings.title: No IndexNow key file implemented
findings.description: The site publishes frequently (draw/news posts, an Express Entry draws page claiming 12-hour auto-updates) but has no IndexNow integration for fast Bing/Yandex indexing.
findings.recommendation: Generate and publish an IndexNow key and wire a ping into the publish pipeline for new/updated content.

findings.title: Duplicate sitemap entry: /noc/72410 listed twice
findings.description: The NOC-code data pipeline emits this URL twice with identical lastmod/priority/changefreq.
findings.recommendation: De-duplicate the source dataset feeding the sitemap generator.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: The blog's evergreen definitional guide (o-que-e-imigracao-guia-completo) has genuine depth (~950-1,050 words), clean H2/H3 structure, a comparison table, and a glossary
Real, differentiated per-article publish dates on the blog (not fabricated, unlike the sitemap)
/dados/brasileiros-express-entry-2026 is a genuinely original-data asset (a real study with specific numbers) — strong authority-building potential if promoted
Calculators/quiz pages already carry solid ~120-140 word standalone declarative explainer text alongside the interactive tools
Keyword usage throughout is natural, not stuffed

findings.title: No About/Sobre page and no legal-entity identity anywhere on the site
findings.description: Only /faq, /precos, /contato, /privacidade, /termos, /blog are linked anywhere. /contato is just a support email with no company name, CNPJ, address, or team. No Organization schema exists. Two different unexplained support emails appear on the site (suporte@ vs. contato@immigracan.com.br). For a YMYL site processing payments, this is one of the most heavily-weighted quality-rater trust signals and is also a Brazilian consumer-protection (CDC) concern.
findings.recommendation: Publish a real /sobre page with legal entity name + CNPJ, founder/team names, physical/mailing address, and one consistent support email; add matching Organization schema.

findings.title: No named author or expertise attribution on any content page
findings.description: Article JSON-LD uses "author":{"@type":"Organization"} sitewide across ~90 blog posts, ~90 NOC pages, ~36 profession pages, and program pages. No byline, bio, or credential appears anywhere, despite the operators clearly understanding the regulatory landscape (they write about CICC rule changes).
findings.recommendation: Add named Person authors with real, disclosed qualifications, or at minimum a credentialed 'reviewed by' for eligibility content; update Article schema to author type Person.

findings.title: The paid R$19.90 AI-generated report has no visible disclaimer or human-review disclosure at the point of sale
findings.description: /precos (99 words) never mentions that the report is AI-generated/unreviewed or that ImmigraCan is not a licensed CICC/RCIC consultant. That disclaimer exists only buried in /termos and inside a collapsed FAQ accordion answer — never at the moment someone is deciding whether to pay.
findings.recommendation: Add a prominent, non-collapsed disclaimer directly on /precos and immediately before checkout.

findings.title: Thin, near-boilerplate content across ~150+ programmatic page templates (NOC, imigrar-como, custo-de-vida, programas, pnp)
findings.description: Per-page unique content is roughly 40-150 words across these ~150 URLs (about half the site) — e.g. custo-de-vida/toronto is ~40-50 unique words, NOC pages ~90-110. These read as data-field lookups wrapped in identical boilerplate rather than genuine guidance.
findings.recommendation: Add substantive unique value per page/family: pathway narratives, pitfalls, sourced figures, cross-links to related content — even 150-250 additional words per page would materially change the picture.

findings.title: Verbatim-template duplicate content across 15+ 'sorteio' draw-result posts and 10+ processing-time update posts
findings.description: Two sampled 'sorteio CEC' posts are word-for-word identical except for date and invite count. This Mad-Libs pattern repeats across at least 25 blog URLs targeting overlapping keywords, risking both a quality read and keyword cannibalization.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate into continuously-updated hub pages (the site already has /express-entry/draws and /historico-draws as models) instead of minting a new near-identical article per event.

findings.title: The FAQ page's real, high-quality answers are invisible to any non-JS crawler and hidden inside a click-to-reveal accordion
findings.description: The best trust-building content on the site — 26 genuinely good Q&A pairs including the honest 'we are not a licensed consultant' answer — exists only in JSON-LD/accordion state, not in visible, crawlable text, and the page's raw HTML actually duplicates the homepage (see Technical findings).
findings.recommendation: Server-render the FAQ answers as visible text, not JS/click-gated; fix the underlying routing bug causing /faq to serve homepage content in raw HTML.

findings.title: RCIC/licensing disclaimer is present on blog posts but absent from the programmatic pages making the most specific actionable claims
findings.description: Present on blog posts; absent on /programas/pnp_ontario, /pnp/ontario, /imigrar-como/eletricista, and critically /precos — the pages stating specific eligibility criteria, salary ranges, and pricing with no caveat.
findings.recommendation: Add the same disclaimer footer used on blog posts to the programas/pnp/noc/imigrar-como templates — one component update covers ~150 URLs.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Title tags are natural, well-formed, and reasonably lengthed (mostly 50-70 chars) across sampled templates
Every one of the 294 crawled pages has exactly one H1 and a canonical tag present
No stray noindex found anywhere on real templates; robots meta correctly index,follow sitewide
Zero images site-wide were found missing alt text in the full 294-page crawl

findings.title: All 90 blog posts (100% of the blog) are missing meta descriptions
findings.description: Confirmed via full-site crawl (crawl-data.psv): every one of the 90 /blog/{slug} URLs has an empty meta description field, while all 204 non-blog pages have one. This is the single largest content section on the site shipping with no SERP/social snippet control at all.
findings.recommendation: Backfill and fix the template default (see Technical SEO H1 for the same finding).

findings.title: 5 sitemap-listed pages self-canonicalize to the homepage instead of themselves
findings.description: /comparador, /prontidao, /templates, and /faq all carry <link rel="canonical" href="https://immigracan.com.br"> in raw HTML rather than pointing at themselves, directly contradicting the sitemap's instruction to index them as distinct URLs.
findings.recommendation: Fix per-route canonical injection (same root cause as the Technical SEO soft-404 finding).

findings.title: /quiz — the core conversion entry point — has no <h1> anywhere in the DOM
findings.description: Confirmed via rendered DOM inspection; the page shows only a breadcrumb and a progress indicator, no page-level heading, which is suboptimal for both accessibility and for signaling page topic to search engines.
findings.recommendation: Add a visually-hidden or small H1 such as 'Quiz de Elegibilidade para Imigrar ao Canadá'.

findings.title: 9 pages share duplicate titles/descriptions (2 duplicate title groups beyond the homepage-cannibalized 5, plus a duplicate NOC page)
findings.description: /express-entry/draws and /express-entry/draws/2026 share an identical title; the duplicate /noc/72410 sitemap entry produces a literal duplicate title/description pair.
findings.recommendation: Differentiate the draws-vs-2026-archive titles; de-duplicate the NOC entry.

findings.title: Blog post H1 duplicates the full <title> including the site-name suffix
findings.description: H1 repeats "... | ImmigraCan" verbatim instead of just the headline — the brand suffix belongs in <title> for SERP branding, not the visible on-page H1.
findings.recommendation: Strip the site-name suffix when rendering H1 on the blog template.

categories.name: Schema / Structured Data
what_works: All JSON-LD found sitewide uses correct @context and is server-rendered in raw HTML (no raw-vs-rendered discrepancy)
NOC (~90), imigrar-como (36), and pnp (12) templates correctly carry matched FAQPage + BreadcrumbList schema
Homepage carries WebSite, FAQPage, and SoftwareApplication/Offer blocks
Express Entry draws pages carry Dataset schema — a good, underused pattern

findings.title: /precos (the pricing/checkout page) has zero structured data
findings.description: Despite listing two real paid tiers (R$19.90 report, R$29.90/mo subscription), there is no Product/Service/Offer markup at all — the single highest-value schema gap on the site given real money changes hands here.
findings.recommendation: Add Service + OfferCatalog (or Product + Offer) JSON-LD describing both paid tiers with real pricing.

findings.title: No Organization schema anywhere on the site
findings.description: Every Organization reference found (in Article.publisher, Article.author, Dataset.creator) is a bare {"@type":"Organization","name":"ImmigraCan"} stub with no @id, logo, sameAs, or founder — Google cannot merge these into one entity, and there's no knowledge-panel-eligible identity for a YMYL site.
findings.recommendation: Add one site-wide Organization block with a real ≥112x112px logo (not favicon.ico) and real sameAs links (omit sameAs entirely rather than inventing profiles that don't exist), referenced by @id elsewhere.

findings.title: Homepage SoftwareApplication is missing aggregateRating (blocking rich-result eligibility) and only represents the free tier
findings.description: Without aggregateRating the page cannot earn the Software App rich result at all; the same defect exists on every WebApplication block on tool pages. Separately, the single Offer for price "0" ignores the two paid products entirely.
findings.recommendation: Do not fabricate ratings — only add aggregateRating once a real rating-collection mechanism exists. Expand offers to an array/AggregateOffer covering all three tiers.

findings.title: Blog Article.author is Organization, not Person; publisher.logo uses favicon.ico; Article.image is a relative URL
findings.description: Three related gaps on the same Article schema: weak E-E-A-T authorship signal, a non-standard .ico image format for the logo property, and a relative (non-absolute) image URL that fails Google's structured-data URL requirements.
findings.recommendation: Use a named Person author (or add reviewedBy), swap the logo to a real PNG/SVG brand asset, and make the image URL absolute.

findings.title: /programas/pnp_{code} template (~18 pages) has zero schema while the sibling /pnp/{province} template has FAQPage+BreadcrumbList
findings.description: Directly inconsistent implementation across two overlapping templates covering the same real-world programs.
findings.recommendation: Port the same FAQPage+BreadcrumbList pattern from /pnp/{province} onto /programas/{id}.

findings.title: No BreadcrumbList on blog posts or on /custo-de-vida/{city} pages (~15 pages)
findings.description: Both are 2+ level-deep URL families that would benefit from Google's breadcrumb rich result replacing the raw URL in the SERP snippet.
findings.recommendation: Add BreadcrumbList to both templates.

findings.title: /calculadora-crs and several other free tools have zero structured data; /quiz uses a non-rich-result Quiz type
findings.description: Only 3 of 9 tool pages carry WebApplication+Offer; /calculadora-crs, /conversor-clb, /simulador-cenarios, /historico-draws, /buscador-noc, and /checklist-documentos have none at all, despite /calculadora-crs likely being the single highest-intent page on the site.
findings.recommendation: Standardize every free-tool page on WebApplication+Offer (Quiz type can be kept in addition via @graph).

findings.title: NOC pages (~90) have no Occupation/DefinedTerm entity markup
findings.description: Each page's core content (NOC code, occupation name, TEER level, EE category) is exactly the kind of fact that benefits from explicit entity markup for AI-answer-engine clarity, even without a Google rich-result surface.
findings.recommendation: Add DefinedTerm/DefinedTermSet markup referencing the NOC 2021 classification.

categories.name: Performance (Core Web Vitals)
what_works: TTFB is consistently good (163-364ms) across every page tested — server response is not a bottleneck
Google Fonts use a correct async preload→swap pattern with a working noscript fallback
GTM/AdSense are deferred via requestIdleCallback rather than blocking the head, and this is confirmed to keep them off the LCP path
DOM size is reasonable (775 elements on homepage, well under the ~1,500 excessive-DOM threshold)

findings.title: SSR-fallback-to-hydration DOM swap causes severe CLS (0.31-0.52, 'Poor') on /quiz and /calculadora-crs — the two primary conversion pages
findings.description: Lighthouse attributes ~100% of the CLS on both pages to the footer jumping into a new position when React replaces the minimal SSR fallback markup with the much-taller real interactive widget.
findings.recommendation: Reserve layout height in the SSR fallback matching the hydrated content's real height, or set a min-height on the wrapping container so hydration only fills in interactivity rather than replacing a short DOM subtree with a tall one.

findings.title: None of the 5 tested pages pass all three Core Web Vitals in this lab run
findings.description: Homepage TBT 1,380ms / max-potential-FID 638ms; blog LCP 4.9s (Poor); quiz and calculadora-crs both fail CLS. Lighthouse performance scores range 51-70.
findings.recommendation: See individual findings below; prioritize the CLS fix (highest severity) and the third-party/hydration main-thread contention fix.

findings.title: Blog LCP (4.9s, Poor) and quiz LCP are distorted by late-mounting fixed overlays (PWA install promo, cookie-consent banner) becoming the LCP element instead of real content
findings.description: The LCP element on the blog page resolves to a position:fixed promotional banner's text, and on /quiz to the cookie-consent banner — both mount after hydration and are large relative to viewport.
findings.recommendation: Mount these overlays earlier (ideally synchronously) and constrain their visual size on mobile so they're not selected as LCP candidates.

findings.title: AdSense script execution directly overlaps React hydration's long tasks on the main thread, producing 1,380ms TBT / 638ms max-potential-FID on the homepage
findings.description: requestIdleCallback fires earlier than intended (mid-hydration) rather than truly after it, stacking AdSense's ~555ms scripting cost directly on top of React's 638ms hydration task.
findings.recommendation: Gate third-party script injection on an explicit 'hydration complete' signal rather than the first available idle slot, or delay AdSense/analytics until after first user interaction.

findings.title: Blog hero image is an unoptimized 308KB PNG with no WebP/AVIF or responsive srcset
findings.description: This single image is 31% of the blog page's total byte weight; a well-optimized WebP/AVIF at the same dimensions should be 75-85% smaller.
findings.recommendation: Re-encode blog feature images as WebP/AVIF with 2-3 responsive srcset widths.

findings.title: Render-blocking CSS bundle (16.2KB) on every page with no critical-CSS inlining
findings.description: Estimated 150-300ms of savings per page available.
findings.recommendation: Inline critical above-the-fold CSS and defer the rest using the same preload pattern already used for fonts.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness (GEO)
what_works: robots.txt currently allows all major AI crawlers (GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, CCBot, anthropic-ai) — good for AI visibility
~150+ NOC/PNP/imigrar-como templated pages carry genuine, well-matched FAQPage + BreadcrumbList schema
Calculators/quiz pages already carry solid standalone declarative explainer text independent of the interactive tools
The Dataset schema pattern on Express Entry draws pages is a good, underused citability asset

findings.title: /faq — the site's richest, most citable Q&A content — is completely invisible to every non-JS-executing AI crawler
findings.description: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, and OAI-SearchBot don't execute JavaScript, so a plain fetch of /faq returns the homepage's content instead (see Technical/On-Page findings), hiding 26 genuinely good Q&A pairs — including the honest 'we are not a licensed consultant' answer — from the exact systems most likely to want to cite it.
findings.recommendation: Add /faq to the same static-generation/prerender path used for the site's other correctly-SSR'd routes; audit the full route list for any other page silently falling back to the homepage shell.

findings.title: The universal soft-200 catch-all disguises the fact that llms.txt does not exist
findings.description: GET /llms.txt returns HTTP 200 with homepage HTML rather than a real 404 or a real file, so a naive status-code check would falsely report it as present.
findings.recommendation: Fix the catch-all to return a real 404/noindex for unmatched paths, then create a real /llms.txt listing the site's content hubs.

findings.title: Homepage FAQPage schema doesn't match any visible on-page text
findings.description: The two schema questions ('O que é o ImmigraCan?', 'O quiz é gratuito?') appear nowhere in the visible homepage body, which is about general immigration definitions instead — a schema/content mismatch that risks rich-result demotion and looks like a manipulation signal to AI quality classifiers.
findings.recommendation: Either add matching visible Q&A text to the homepage or remove/relocate this specific FAQPage block (the real FAQ content lives on /faq).

findings.title: None of the ~150+ templated pages use question-phrased headings
findings.description: Every category uses statement-style H2s ('Elegibilidade no Express Entry') instead of question form, despite the question phrasing already existing in each page's own FAQPage Question.name fields — a cheap, high-leverage citability lever currently unused.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite heading templates to question form, reusing text already written for the schema — a template-level change that cascades to ~150 pages at once.

findings.title: No Organization schema and no sameAs/social profile links found anywhere — near-zero externally-verifiable entity presence
findings.description: An LLM asked whether ImmigraCan is a trustworthy source today has almost nothing to corroborate it with beyond the site's own text; the only social reference is an unlinked twitter:site meta tag.
findings.recommendation: Add sitewide Organization JSON-LD with real sameAs links, publish a static /sobre page, and prioritize a real off-site presence (e.g. YouTube) over backlink volume.

findings.title: A freshness claim is contradicted by live data on /express-entry/draws
findings.description: The page claims automatic updates every 12 hours, but the underlying data endpoint's latest draw date was roughly 7 weeks stale at audit time.
findings.recommendation: Fix the update job or soften the on-page freshness claim to match actual cadence, and add dateModified to the Dataset schema.

categories.name: Images
what_works: Zero images site-wide were found missing alt text across the full 294-page crawl
Explicit width/height attributes are set on the blog hero image, preventing its own layout shift
No hotlinking to external image hosts was observed despite a leftover Unsplash dns-prefetch hint
loading="eager" is correctly used for the above-the-fold blog hero image

findings.title: Blog hero images are unoptimized (308KB PNG) with no modern format or responsive delivery
findings.description: This is the largest single network transfer on blog pages (31% of total byte weight); no AVIF/WebP variant and no srcset for mobile clients.
findings.recommendation: Re-encode as WebP/AVIF with 2-3 responsive widths; target 30-80KB at these dimensions.

findings.title: Money pages (quiz, calculators, pricing) carry almost no imagery at all
findings.description: No CRS score-breakdown visual, no sample-report screenshot, no city cost-of-living map/comparison graphic — a missed trust/comprehension opportunity on exactly the pages where visual proof would help conversion most.
findings.recommendation: Add at least a sample-report screenshot on /precos and simple comparison visuals on high-value tool/data pages.

findings.title: Unused images.unsplash.com dns-prefetch hint
findings.description: Zero requests to this origin were observed across all pages tested — the hint is currently pure waste.
findings.recommendation: Remove the hint, or confirm it's needed on an untested route.

additional_categories.name: Search Experience (SXO)
additional_categories.note: Not part of the weighted health score; supplements Content Quality and On-Page SEO with SERP-backwards page-type/intent analysis.
additional_categories.primary_finding: CRITICAL page-type/intent mismatch: /precos sells an unlicensed AI-generated report with zero trust signals, while the SERPs for the two most commercially-adjacent queries ('consultor de imigração canadá', 'quanto custa imigrar para o canadá') are dominated by licensed RCIC/lawyer service pages and itemized real-cost blog posts respectively — neither intent is credibly served.

additional_categories.name: Content Architecture / Clustering
additional_categories.note: Not part of the weighted health score; supplements Content Quality and Technical SEO with hub-and-spoke and cannibalization analysis.
additional_categories.primary_finding: The Ontario PNP keyword space is split across 4 URLs with a live factual contradiction (one page says the program is active, others correctly say revoked); the NOC hub (/buscador-noc, ~90 spokes) contains zero links to any spoke page; ~25 recurring 'sorteio'/processing-time blog posts cannibalize each other and their own intended canonical pages.

additional_categories.name: Visual / Mobile
additional_categories.note: Not part of the weighted health score; supplements Performance and On-Page SEO with real-browser rendering checks.
additional_categories.primary_finding: The blog's client-side API is broken in production (GET /api/blog returns [], GET /api/blog/{slug} returns 404), so every blog post renders 'Erro ao carregar artigo' to real visitors despite good server-rendered HTML. The LGPD cookie-consent banner also covers 35-45% of the mobile viewport and hides the Premium plan CTA on desktop /precos without scrolling.

additional_categories.name: Backlinks / Authority
additional_categories.note: Not part of the weighted health score (Tier 0 data only — no Moz/Bing/DataForSEO configured); reported as insufficient data rather than a fabricated score.
additional_categories.primary_finding: immigracan.com.br is entirely absent from Common Crawl's web graph (not merely low-ranked), consistent with a young, 2026-launched domain. No sameAs entries, no discoverable social profile links, and no verifiable referring domains were found through any free-tier source.

phases.name: Phase 1: Critical Fixes
items: Fix the broken blog backend (/api/blog and /api/blog/{slug} currently return empty/404) so real visitors stop seeing 'Erro ao carregar artigo' on every one of the 90 blog posts

Fix the soft-404 architecture: return a real HTTP 404 for unknown routes, and add /faq, /templates, /comparador, /prontidao to the SSR/prerender route list so they stop serving the homepage's title/description/canonical/JSON-LD
Add a prominent, non-collapsed disclaimer on /precos and at checkout stating the report is AI-generated and ImmigraCan is not a licensed RCIC/CICC consultant
Correct the factual error on /programas/pnp_ontario ('Status: Ativo') to reflect the real OINP revocation (30 May 2026)
Fix plain-HTTP (port 80) to 301-redirect to HTTPS instead of dead-ending on a bare 404
Add site-wide Organization JSON-LD (real logo, real sameAs only — no fabricated profiles) and Service/Offer schema to /precos

phases.name: Phase 2: High-Impact Improvements
items: Backfill meta description/og:description/twitter:description on all 90 blog posts and fix the template default
Fix absolute vs. relative og:image/Article.image URLs on the blog template
Reserve layout height in the SSR fallback for /quiz and /calculadora-crs to eliminate the 0.31-0.52 CLS from the hydration DOM swap
Re-time AdSense/analytics script injection so it stops overlapping React hydration's main-thread work (homepage TBT 1,380ms)
Add a named Person author (or reviewedBy) to Article schema; publish a real /sobre page with legal entity name, CNPJ, and team info
Add BreadcrumbList to blog posts and /custo-de-vida/{city}; port FAQPage+BreadcrumbList from /pnp/{province} onto /programas/{id}
Add WebApplication/Offer schema to /calculadora-crs and the other schema-less tool pages
Fix the four late-mounting fixed overlays (cookie banner, PWA promo) that are distorting LCP measurements and covering CTAs on mobile/desktop
Add X-Frame-Options / begin a CSP Report-Only rollout

phases.name: Phase 3: Content & Authority
items: Consolidate the ~25 recurring 'sorteio'/processing-time blog posts into continuously-updated hub pages instead of a new near-identical article per event
Add substantive unique content to the ~150 thin programmatic pages (NOC, imigrar-como, custo-de-vida, programas, pnp) — pathway narratives, sourced figures, cross-links
Fix the NOC hub (/buscador-noc) to link forward to its ~90 spoke pages; add /pnp, /buscador-noc, /custo-de-vida, /imigrar-como to global navigation
Rewrite the ~150 templated page headings into question form, reusing existing FAQPage Question.name text
Add cross-links between related clusters (profession → NOC → PNP → city cost-of-living)
Re-encode blog hero images as WebP/AVIF with responsive srcset
Build a real off-site brand presence (Organization sameAs targets) and begin digital-PR/link-building now that the domain has content worth linking to

phases.name: Phase 4: Monitoring & Iteration
items: Stop stamping sitemap lastmod with the build date on non-blog URLs; only update on real content changes
Set up a regression check: for every sitemap URL, fetch raw HTML and confirm the title matches the expected page (catches future soft-404 regressions automatically)
Get a free Moz API key and verify the domain in Bing Webmaster Tools to start measuring backlinks (currently absent from Common Crawl entirely)
Re-run Core Web Vitals measurement with real CrUX/PSI field data once Google API credentials are configured
Audit the remaining PNP province pairs (BC, Alberta, Quebec, Atlantic) for the same live/revoked factual-contradiction pattern found on Ontario
